speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) from 2016 to date, how many appeals on re-employment disputes has the Ministry received annually; (b) how many of these appeals are successful; and (c) what are the main reasons for unsuccessful appeals.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked the Minister for Manpower regarding re-employment disputes reported in 2016 to 2020 (a) how many notifications have been received by the Commissioner for Labour under section 8A of the Retirement and Re-employment Act (RRA); (b) of these cases, how many and what proportion are subsequently referred to the Minister for decision under section 8B of the RRA after conciliation failed; and (c) what proportion of cases are found to be substantiated.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked the Minister for Manpower regarding re-employment disputes reported in 2016 to 2020, of the cases where the employee succeeded in obtaining compensation under sections 8A and 8B of the Retirement and Re-employment Act, how many cases was the errant employer a public sector employer.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The remaining 10% were either escalated to the Minister for Manpower for a decision on unreasonable denial of re-employment, or to the Employment Claims Tribunals (ECT) for disputes over re-employment terms, or quantum of employment assistance payment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There was only one such case involving a public sector employer in 2018.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: To avoid disputes over re-employment, employers and employees should refer to the Retirement and Re-employment Act and the Tripartite Guidelines on the Re-employment of Older Employees.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Employers should engage senior employees as early as possible to discuss possible re-employment arrangements.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Senior employees should also be open to alternative jobs and reskilling opportunities to improve their long-term employability.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Many are reluctant to even try looking for work because of their bad experiences with age discrimination.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Age discrimination is in the workplace is rooted in ageism, which is an attitude of the heart.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can MOM embark on a more extensive and sustainable public education and engagement campaign to ingrain into the mindsets of everyone in Singapore, that age discrimination is morally, socially and legally unacceptable and, ultimately, hurts the ability of companies to attract and retain good workers?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned some numbers – he said 80 cases have been adjudicated.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The fact that there are so few cases being adjudicated points to either two things: one, there is very little age discrimination in Singapore, or two, older workers are not confident that the process will achieve their desired results.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: So, can the Ministry look into improving the reporting and appeals process, to better assist older workers who have experienced age discrimination?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is not going to be something that we can do in a short period of time, because sometimes this messaging does take a while to percolate.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And unfortunately, I think that sometimes until a person reaches a point where he or she faces that dilemma or the issue, some people may not be open to seek information or receive educational materials, when the thing comes.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We are working actively through the unions who are representatives within the companies to also be a bit of a gatekeeper on how employers take care of the older workers within the company.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This tripartite effort will continue to be played out over the many years to come.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The employment rate of residents aged between 55 and 64 has increased from 61.2% in the year 2011 to 69% in 2021.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For those aged 65 to 69, it has also increased from 35.2% in 2011 to 49% in 2021.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This is comparable to those of the top three Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, while Mr Giam may have anecdotally encountered residents who do have grievances, or perhaps, are not aware of their rights and find that they have been disadvantaged, the fact is that over the last many years, the labour force participation rates in our older workforce has actually increased.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it shows that more employers are prepared to employ older workers, and more older workers are also flexible enough and prepared to take on jobs and continue in the employment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But as it is, there will always be a few cases a year, who will find that they have either a mismatched expectation between the employment terms they seek or for which employers may still have misunderstanding about how they can better employ older workers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There are many avenues in which workers can seek redress.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: One, of course, is through their union representative in their company.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Two, the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) is always there as a neutral party to receive any complaints from employees, or senior workers about the terms of disengagement, or any of the re-employment terms that they may feel is unfair.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They can write to us if they find that they are denied unjustifiably of re-employment opportunities.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Two supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The first relates to cases that were decided by the Minister to be substantiated under section 8B of the Act.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Am I right to assume that the compensation amount is usually a multiple of the employees' last drawn salary?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And if that is the case, could the Ministry share with us: so far, what has been the range of the compensations ordered by the Minister, in terms of how many months?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: And the second supplementary question is, it was announced in 2021 that anti-discrimination legislation would be worked upon.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Does he have any update for us on this and when we can expect it to come into force.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There is a fixed formula which is used; so, it is not something that we just pluck a number out of thin air.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But for each of these quantum, there is a certain minimum and maximum that is stipulated in the formula.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, again, there are no immediate updates at this moment, but at a suitable juncture in time when the discussions are more final, we will provide an update to the Members of the House.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Just to clarify the Senior Minister of State's answer on the first question.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: In his answer, he mentioned the Employment Assistance Payment (EAP).

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But my concern was more about those cases where they were unreasonably denied re-employment, which is more a case of compensation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: There are cases in which the employer may have to bear some responsibility, and there are cases in which also the employee himself or herself has got to bear part of the responsibility for, perhaps, not communicating, or not performing, or not indicating his or her interest to further the re-employment contract.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, in that sense, we take into account a myriad of factors: performance of the employee, years of service and including other aspects of the job scope, what were the terms of re-employment that were being offered, whether it was a fair description of the job that a person can meaningfully carry on.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I hope that kind of gives the Member a sense of how we look at it in terms of the matrix.
